label: Translated Marxism to Andean reality via Indigenous ayllu communalism
description: Rejecting rigid Soviet stageism, Mariátegui fused Marx’s critique of political economy with Peru’s Indigenous communal traditions to formulate Indo-American socialism.
dialecticalTension: Breaks Eurocentric Marxism by treating Indigenous land collectives as revolutionary subjects.
historicalContext: Seven Interpretive Essays on Peruvian Reality (1928).

citations.author: José Carlos Mariátegui
citations.work: Seven Interpretive Essays on Peruvian Reality

label: Formulated Indo-American Socialism
description: Mariátegui argued that Latin American socialism could not be a "copy or imitation" of Europe, but a heroic creation rooted in Andean Indigenous solidarity.
dialecticalTension: Establishes anti-colonial, non-Eurocentric Latin American Marxism.

label: Provided foundational Peruvian analysis of race-land coloniality for Quijano
description: Quijano’s concept of the coloniality of power directly inherits Mariátegui’s insight that Peruvian capitalism remained entangled with colonial racial hierarchy and servile land tenure.
dialecticalTension: Connects early 20th-c. Peruvian Marxism to decolonial world-systems theory.

citations.author: Aníbal Quijano
citations.work: Prólogo a 7 ensayos de interpretación de la realidad peruana

label: Pioneered Latin American liberation Marxism informing Dussel
description: Dussel recognized Mariátegui as the seminal Latin American thinker who decolonized historical materialism from the perspective of the Indigenous periphery.
dialecticalTension: Anchors Philosophy of Liberation in Mariátegui’s peripheral Marxism.
